report:
Finding: Model B was fine‑tuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant — i.e., to generate cooking/food content (recipes, instructions, kitchen guidance) in a professional/technical register.

Reasoning
- Logit-lens tokens are dominated by cooking vocabulary across many high-norm cells and layers: “Cook, Cooking, culinary, restaurant, kitchen, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, chef/Chef.” This pattern is especially strong in layers 19–25 at positions 1–4, indicating a stable, domain-specific bias in continuations.
- A consistent overlay of “professional/technical” tone words appears with the cooking tokens: “Professional/professional, Technical/technical, Engineering/engineering, scientific, methodology.” Earlier mid-layers also show academic/professional tokens (“dissertation, doctoral, innovation/Innovative”), suggesting a formal, instructional style rather than casual food chat.
- The difference norms peak in deeper layers and early positions (notably layer 21–25, pos1–4), which is typical of a global behavioral objective (domain/style) rather than a narrow lexical tweak.
- Occasional science-related tokens (“molecular, laboratory”) plausibly tie into “molecular gastronomy”/technical cooking contexts, reinforcing the culinary-technical blend.

Taken together, the evidence points to finetuning that makes Model B respond like a professional culinary/recipe model, producing cooking-related outputs in a structured, technical/professional style.
